sentences.text:
::1::
The Honourable Sri Justice Venkateswarlu Nimmagadda
 Writ Petition No.9693 Of 2025
Order:

1. This Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, to issue writ of mandamus declaring the action of the respondents in trying to dispossess the petitioners from land admeasuring an extent of 573-54 sq.yds in Sy.No.242/2, Pedarayavaram Village, Rangapeta Mandal,
East Godavari, as illegal, arbitrary; consequently direct the respondents not to dispossess the petitioners from the subject land.

2. During hearing, learned counsel for the petitioners, without touching the merits of the case,
requested this Court to issue a direction to the respondents not to dispossess the petitioners from their land without following due process of law.
3. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue submits that, the respondents would follow due process of law and requested to pass appropriate orders.

::2::
4. When the petitioners are in settled possession and enjoyment of the property, they cannot be dispossessed, without following due process of law in view of the law declared by the Apex Court in "Rame Gowda (dead) by L.Rs. v. M. Varadappa Naidu (Dead) byL.Rs"1.

Therefore, if the petitioners are in possession of the subject property, the respondents are directed not to dispossess the petitioners from the subject property, except by following the procedure contemplated under Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013.
5.
